title: planning: one flow from business request to release, ports for task and spec, reason to exist in README
description:
Intent (settled with the person in grilling, 2026-10-11/12): one planning flow for a solo developer who ships CLIs, desktop apps, component libraries and Claude marketplaces, where the person plays product owner, tech lead and reviewer and the agent drafts everything. Modelled on Anthropic's AI-native SDLC playbook (intent -> spec -> plan -> PR), with plan.md replaced by spec plus tasks.md.

Flow and decisions:
1. Business request: the first messages of a conversation, before an intent exists. Not stored apart; the session archive holds it.
2. Grilling (product owner level: what it does, how it behaves, how it looks) produces the intent of the work, written into a br epic with its acceptance criteria. Gate: the person's yes.
3. Plan (tech lead level): the epic is split into pieces; each piece gets one br task under the epic and its own OpenSpec change (proposal, spec deltas, design: where things go, basic abstractions). The task is created with the spec, never before. Gate: the person's yes to the spec.
4. tasks.md of the change is the developer's local breakdown of that one task (files, order, proof); subtasks never go into br. Gate: the person's yes before code.
5. Apply, review through the review agent, push. Archive closes the change's task.
6. Every epic has acceptance criteria and a final test-it task that runs the real path end to end. The epic closes only when all its tasks are done, every acceptance criterion holds, the test-it task passed, and the work is pushed after review.
7. A fix: a commit only (its why in the message); no epic, task or spec.
8. Wayfinder is merged into the epic: open decisions of large work are child tasks of kind decision, settled by grilling. The wayfinder skill is removed.
9. Ports, not tools: plan names the roles task and spec, never br or OpenSpec. The task port is a new plug-in qsm-tasks (the task-tool skill leaves qsm-essentials, the br install leaves qsm-plan); the spec port is qsm-openspec. qsm-plan requires both as declared dependencies with reasons (AGENTS.md, Architecture rule 2); no fallback.
10. Reason to exist: a project's or plugin's permanent reason for existing becomes the first README section "## Why it exists", five sentences at most, held by a validate gate. INTENT.md files are removed. "Intent" now means only the intent of a piece of work, in its epic.
11. No fallbacks, compatibility or history (rules/implementation.md, "One path").

Acceptance criteria:
- qsm-plan's skills and spec describe steps 1-8 and name ports only; the wayfinder skill is gone.
- qsm-tasks exists with the task skill rewritten to this model, the br install and a doctor; qsm-essentials and qsm-plan no longer hold either.
- qsm-openspec creates the change's br task with the spec and treats tasks.md as the local breakdown.
- Every plugin and the root README open with "## Why it exists" (<= 5 sentences, gate enforced); no INTENT.md is left; AGENTS.md, the generated instructions, add-plugin and the console read the new place.
- The console shows each plugin's reason to exist, its dependencies with their reasons, and the epics and tasks that name it.
- A test-it run: a fresh session plans one small real feature through the whole flow and every gate asks.

An agent that knows the code (the orchestrator or the implementer) must not define what tests test, because that ends with thousands of tests, half of which test the runtime or the language.
Why: companion to the rule that tests prove real edge cases and the intended use only (feedback qsm-i1u.35).

title: qsm-secrets: askpass popouts in Quickshell for secrets and sudo
description:
Intent: an agent that needs a secret or root never sees the value and never needs a terminal: a floating Quickshell pane asks the person, the value goes straight to the vault (secret) or to sudo (authorize). Pinentry-qt works through the same protocol but looks generic; the person wants their own panes. The QML modules live in the qsm-secrets plugin, not in qsm-desktop.
Design: qsm-askpass (bun binary in qsm-secrets) opens a one-shot 0600 unix socket in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, calls 'qs ipc call askpass show <request json without value>', the pane writes the reply only to the socket. Kinds: Secret (blue, key icon, 'Claude wants to set secret <key>', masked field, Save/Cancel), Authorize (orange/red, shield, the exact command read from /proc/<ppid>/cmdline and unwrapped with shell-ast, password + Allow/Deny), Decide (later: hook-kit HOOK_KIT_ASKPASS ask decisions, Allow/Deny only). One path: qs not running or IPC target missing is 'missing', no fallback to pinentry or a terminal. Timeout 120 s is 'timeout', cancel is 'cancelled'. Switch: qsm-secrets askpass enable --secrets --sudo sets SUDO_ASKPASS and adds an ai-guardrails rule that refuses sudo without -A; recommend timestamp_timeout=0 so sudo cache does not skip the pane.
Threat model: protects values from the transcript, logs and the model, and makes secret entry and command authorization visually distinct; it does not stop an agent running as the same uid from spoofing a pane (peer credentials on the socket unverified in Quickshell): state it as a known gap.
Acceptance: qsm-secrets set <key> --gui stores a value typed into the Secret pane and prints nothing; sudo -A true from an agent shell shows the Authorize pane with 'true' and succeeds only after Allow; the value never appears in the Claude transcript (checked with qsm-secrets scrub dry-run); both panes run in the person's live Hyprland session.
Findings to fix in the same epic: (1) plugins/qsm-secrets/hooks/register.tsx:147 lets the prompt through unchanged when capture fails: fail closed instead; (2) has/list/inspect/rm only take an rbw --folder and cannot see the 'capture' namespace on the libsecret backend, so a captured value cannot be listed or removed (seen with cap_ad78dbe04200, a fake test token left in the vault).

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text:
Decision (user): binary integrity via two hashes, at a level that stops the common case, not a determined attacker.
1. Source hash: the git tree hash of a plugin's directory, recorded at install. It answers 'is this bin outdated'. qsm-setup rebuilds only plugins whose source hash changed, on the user's ask (rolling update).
2. Binary hash: sha256 of each installed bin, recorded at install. It answers 'was this bin replaced'. The Quickshell panel reads the caller's /proc/<pid>/exe, hashes it, and refuses with a notification when it does not match. The user can then stop the agent and run the rolling update.
Open: the hash file and the bin dir live under the same user the agent runs as, so an agent could rewrite both. Mitigation: an ai-guardrails deny rule on writes to the hash file and the bin dir. Still open: a fake panel window spawned by the agent itself; out of scope for now.
Unverified: whether bun build --compile is byte-reproducible. If not, the binary hash cannot be compared with a fresh build, only with the hash recorded at install.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Decision (user): hashes are fully static and generated. Every direct write path to the hash file and the bin dir is blocked by a deny rule. Only the update generates new hashes, and the update runs only on the user's ask. Requirement that follows: the update's 'ask' must come from the person, not the agent. The Authorize pane confirms it, the same way it confirms sudo; otherwise an agent can run the update itself and re-bless a replaced bin.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Finding: gnome-keyring-daemon on this machine aborts (core dump, GLib invoke_get_property_in_idle_cb assertion) when a client reads Secret.Item properties over D-Bus (busctl get-property Label/Attributes/Locked); each restart relocks the keyring. Any askpass or qsm-secrets code goes through secret-tool, never raw D-Bus property reads.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Built overnight (6a902253, b11cd8b5, dc3706ed, on main 83dfe42a): one pane (qml/askpass, Kinds.js table) and providers secret/sudo/ssh/git/decide/notice, links qsm-askpass-<kind>, set --gui, askpass enable (prints fish lines), guard refuses askpass-pane calls from agent Bash. Proven live on Hyprland with an own qs instance: secret stored via the fake backend, Escape cancels, decide shows a 600-char request whole. Left for the person: sudo -A true with the real password (Authorize pane, Allow), and enabling SUDO_ASKPASS via the printed fish lines.

The owner and agent need the reviewed Images, Videos, News, Music, Map, Files and Social media source sets selectable through the existing qsm-web search command and correctly taught by its SearXNG skill. Research qsm-r7s7 is complete and independently approved. The owner requested one OpenAI GPT-6 Luna high implementer per profile. Each must reuse the current profile/preflight/request path, not create a new framework.

## Settled decisions
Use images, videos, news, music, map, files and social-media. Social-media includes the eight reviewed sources plus already accepted boardreader. The owner explicitly includes naver news alongside the four clean News candidates and retains its diagnostics. Existing default, niche, academic and it remain unchanged. Other is not a profile; no duplicate Science preset. Implementation belongs to qsm-web CLI/contracts, its skill and user docs. SearXNG server review is a later separate step, not authorization to edit it now.

## Done when
- Each new profile selects exactly its written reviewed engine set, requires all names registered, and never silently substitutes sources.

## Not in this work
No Browserbox work, SearXNG deployment/preferences changes, provider repairs, General replacement, Science/Other profiles, new subprofiles, new dependencies, model eval runs while paused, or blanket content/protocol exclusions. No media/full-text downloads or playback. Keep live verification bounded and respect observed cooldowns.

title: qsm-web: select named engine sets with one profile flag
description:
People and agents need one flag for a named source selection. The current profile and category flags select sources differently, which makes the same-looking request ambiguous. Keep --profile for default, niche, academic and the reviewed IT set, and remove category input without an alias.

## Before and after
| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| --profile it | Usage error | Exact reviewed IT engine set |
| --category it | Server category defaults | Usage error before network access |
| --profile default | Server defaults | Server defaults |

## Not in this work
No server settings, access-challenge repairs, new accounts, catalog pruning, remaining-tab reviews or full engine-catalog skill. No model eval runs while the hold remains open.

## Done when
- [ ] IT selects exactly the 36 engines in the approved change spec and requires every engine to be registered.
- [ ] Category input is absent from CLI and generated noun contracts and is rejected before network access. Result category metadata remains.
- [ ] Existing profiles, manual engines, filters, warning behavior and the shared deadline retain their contracts.
- [ ] Real-entry tests and a compiled CLI run prove selection and failures. Ordinary checks and one independent review pass.
- [ ] The reviewed change is merged and pushed, and the installed command is verified from main.

## Decision
Keep profile because named presets already use it. Keeping category alongside profile leaves two competing selection paths. Renaming all presets to category adds churn without improving the contract.

## Budget
One bounded change in qsm-web, reusing the profile preflight and request path. No new abstraction or command.

title: qsm-memory: pack transcripts no longer in use into a monthly archive, counted in days of use
description:
Intent (the person, 2026-10-30, session 6c7fc7b0): Claude Code transcripts on this machine must never be lost, also not when the person comes back after a long break, and while the person works every day the old ones are packed small. Who: the person, one machine. What: qsm-memory moves transcripts that are no longer in use into a monthly zstd archive beside its database; nothing is deleted without an archive, and a packed session comes back with one tar command. Why now: an old qsm-memory value (cleanupPeriodDays 7) let Claude Code delete every transcript older than a week, at the first start; Claude Code's own default deletes after 30 calendar days, so a break of a month loses everything. The person in their words: "kdyz si vezmu volno, tak muzu treba psat v jedne nebo dvou sessions. Takze sessions musi mit nejaky ticking ... A tento rule se spusti jen kdyz jsem byl active using."

The rule (settled 2026-10-30):
- A day of use is a day on which at least one main session started (read from the qsm-memory archive).
- Each transcript's clock ticks only on days of use after its last change (mtime); a day with one or two sessions on vacation is one tick, a day without Claude Code is none. A transcript with 7 or more ticks is out.
- The activity gate: the pack runs only when at least 3 of the last 5 days were days of use, so after a return the person has at least 3 working days to reopen what is relevant (reopening resets its clock).
- At most once per 30 days, started by the session.start hook (detached, like save), never in the first 30 days after activation. No timer.
- Pack: the transcript and its <session>/ directory (subagents, tool-results) go into ~/.local/share/qsm-memory/transcripts/<YYYY-MM>.tar.zst at zstd -19 (measured: 186 MB of transcripts -> 26 MB); the archive is listed and compared before any original is removed. Restore is tar --zstd -xf, no new verb. show --full of a packed session fails with a code naming the archive and the unpack command.
- Activation offers two modes: qsm (cleanupPeriodDays 36500 and the pack) or Claude Code's default (qsm writes nothing). The doctor reports either as the person's choice; today's rule "any value below 36500 is failed" changes to apply only in qsm mode.

Not: no deletion without an archive, no timer, no monthly question to the agent or the person, no packing of memory.db, no packing in Claude Code mode.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Activation offers both modes; qsm writes 36500 and turns the pack on; Claude Code mode writes nothing; the doctor reports either as a choice, not failed.
2. In the first 30 days after activation, and within 30 days of the last pack, a run moves nothing.
3. With fewer than 3 days of use in the last 5 days, the pack is skipped and the log says why.
4. A run moves exactly the transcripts (and their <session>/ directories) with 7 or more ticks into one <YYYY-MM>.tar.zst at zstd -19, and removes the originals only after the archive is checked.
5. The person's scenarios, on a sandbox of real transcripts: Monday, a week of vacation, Monday: the Monday session stays; a vacation with two sessions adds two ticks to the others, not seven; after a return, nothing is packed in the first 3 days of use.
6. Outside judge: tar --zstd -xf of the archive into ~/.claude/projects, then claude --resume <id> opens the packed session.

title: qsm-cockpit: the loop at a glance
description: Intent: the person sees at a glance which step of the loop the main chat is in (said by the agent through the stage tool, never inferred), every running agent with its model tier in colour and the command it runs, the claimed tasks, and the decisions grouped under the prompt they answered; the agent always knows its step from one line of context per prompt. Not doing: judging the work or moving the loop by itself. Acceptance: (1) after install in a fresh session the band and /cockpit show the step, agents, tasks and decisions; (2) the agent calls stage on each step without being told in the chat; (3) a pane opened late shows the whole session; (4) no tool call or spawn is ever blocked by the plugin. Built: plugin qsm-cockpit, merged into rewrite at b6c0d126.

title: grilling: what qsm-ccr IS — CCR vs ccx scope, provider set, config surface
description:
GRILLING TICKET. Run with the user, one session, before any qsm-ccr file exists. The parent
qsm-brain-collapse-map-g58.10 already carries ten settled facts from the 2026-08-28 build session —
do not relearn them and do not re-decide them. This ticket settles only what that session left open.

The parent's comment of 2026-08-29 names three open questions. They are restated here with the
reason each one changes the tool's shape.

1. CCR vs ccx — what is the deliverable?
   Two things were built by hand on 2026-08-28: the claude-code-router daemon with its sqlite
   config, and ~/.zsh-functions/ccx.sh, a shell function that launches Claude Code against that
   daemon with per-model context and tier envs. They are separable. A tool that sets up only the
   daemon is useful to anyone; a tool that also ships ccx.sh assumes zsh and one person's shell
   layout. Decide whether qsm-ccr owns one, the other, or both behind a flag.
   WHY it changes the shape: if ccx.sh is in scope, the tool needs a shell-integration surface and
   a machine-local install path, which is the whole of sibling ticket "where does ccx.sh land".

2. Which providers ship configured, and which are documented only?
   Settled: codex-api via `codex login` OAuth is the anchor provider. Also present on the built
   machine: OpenRouter and Zen as plain api_key entries, keys through qsm-secret. Decide whether
   the installer writes those two provider rows (requiring a secret to exist at install time), or
   whether it writes only codex-api and documents the rest.
   WHY it changes the shape: writing them means the installer must handle "secret not present yet"
   as a normal path, not an error, or the install is not idempotent on a fresh machine.

3. What is the config surface the user edits?
   The live config is a JSON blob inside sqlite (~/.claude-code-router/config.sqlite, table
   app_config, key 'default', column value_json) — NOT a file the user can edit. Decide whether
   qsm-ccr owns a neutral source-of-truth file it renders into sqlite, or whether it only writes
   sqlite once and then gets out of the way.
   WHY it changes the shape: a rendered config means the tool must handle drift (the daemon
   rewrites parts of that blob on start), which is a different tool from a one-shot writer.

Also settle, because the parent lists them as facts without deciding their scope:

4. Does the tool ship a doctor verb, and what does it assert? Candidate assertions from the build

title: decision: how the scope='ccr' guard is set before the daemon ever starts
description:
DECISION TICKET. The single highest-cost mistake found in the 2026-08-28 build session, recorded on
the parent as settled fact (4):

  "CRITICAL: profile.profiles[agent=claude-code] ships scope='global' and REWRITES
  ~/.claude/settings.json env on every daemon start — must set scope='ccr' + enabled=false BEFORE
  first daemon start (this broke the user's live sessions 3x)"

Read that failure mode plainly, because it decides the tool's whole install order. claude-code-router
ships a profile whose scope is 'global'. When the daemon starts, that profile writes environment
variables into the user's ~/.claude/settings.json. Any Claude Code session already running, or
started later, picks up those variables and routes through the daemon whether or not the user asked
for it. On 2026-08-28 this happened three times before the cause was found.

So the install has an ordering constraint that a normal installer does not have: the config must be
correct BEFORE the daemon is ever started, including the very first start that `bun add -g` or a
first `ccr` invocation might trigger. An installer that starts the daemon to create the config, then
fixes the config, has already caused the damage.

What must be decided:

1. How does the installer write the sqlite config without starting the daemon?
   The config lives at ~/.claude-code-router/config.sqlite, table app_config, key 'default', column
   value_json. If that file does not exist before first start, the installer has to create the
   schema itself, which couples qsm-ccr to a schema it does not own and which upstream may change.
   The alternative is to let the daemon create it, kill the daemon, patch, restart — which accepts
   one window where settings.json is rewritten. Neither option is free. Pick one and record why.

2. What proves the guard held?
   Decide the check that runs after install and after every daemon start: read
   profile.profiles[agent=claude-code].scope and .enabled out of the blob and assert 'ccr' /
   false. Decide whether that check also belongs in a doctor verb, and whether it should refuse to
   report success while ~/.claude/settings.json contains daemon-injected env.

3. What does the tool do when it finds the damage already done?
   A machine where this already fired has ANTHROPIC_* env in ~/.claude/settings.json that the user
   did not put there. Decide whether qsm-ccr removes it, reports it, or refuses to proceed. Removing
   another tool's writes from the user's settings file is destructive and needs an explicit
   decision, not a default.

WHY this is a separate ticket from the grilling ticket: the grilling ticket settles what the tool
IS. This settles a named, measured failure that any shape of the tool has to survive, and its answer
constrains install ordering, which is the first thing the spec has to state.
acceptance_criteria: Three answers recorded on this issue with reasons: (1) how the sqlite config is written without a daemon start, or which damage window is accepted and why; (2) the exact assertion that proves the guard held, and where it runs; (3) what the tool does on a machine where settings.json already carries daemon-injected env — remove, report, or refuse. The install ordering constraint is stated in one sentence the spec can quote verbatim.

title: decision: where ccx.sh lands without hardcoding a machine path, and which shells it serves
description:
DECISION TICKET. Only in play if the grilling ticket puts ccx.sh in scope.

Settled fact (8) on the parent describes what was built by hand on 2026-08-28:

  "~/.zsh-functions/ccx.sh: default sol, shorthand args, per-model CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS,
  tier envs haiku->mini sonnet->terra opus->sol (subagent plumbing only), daemon ensure via port
  probe"

Every part of that path is machine-specific. `~/.zsh-functions/` is one person's zsh layout. Iron
Law 11 and docs/content-layers.md keep concrete machine paths out of this public repository, so the
installer cannot contain that string.

What must be decided:

1. How does the installer learn where shell functions go?
   Candidates, none picked: an environment variable the user sets; a value in the qsm setup state
   file (~/.config/qsm/setup.json, already the canonical setup state per adapters/claude/CLAUDE.md);
   a prompt at install time; or XDG-style detection with a documented default. Each has a different
   idempotency story — a prompt is not idempotent in a scripted install, and detection is not
   idempotent across shells.

2. Which shells are supported?
   The built artefact is zsh. The repository already has qsm-langdev-fish, qsm-langdev-zsh and
   qsm-langdev-shell, so a fish user is a real case here. Decide whether qsm-ccr ships one POSIX
   function sourced by both, per-shell variants, or zsh only with the limitation stated in
   INSTALL.md.

3. Is the model-to-tier mapping config or code?
   Fact (8) hardcodes haiku->mini, sonnet->terra, opus->sol, and fact (7) lists the codex-api model
   set (gpt-5.6-sol/luna/terra at 368k ctx, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini at 256k, gpt-reserve,
   codex-auto-review at 272k). That model list is upstream's and will change. A hardcoded mapping in
   the shell function drifts silently the first time a model is renamed. Decide whether the mapping
   lives in the tool's own config, is derived from `codex debug models` at install time, or is
   accepted as hardcoded with a doctor check that flags a missing model.

4. Does the tool own uninstall?
   A shell function installed into a user's dotfiles is something the tool wrote into a file it does
   not own. Decide whether qsm-ccr removes it on uninstall, and if so how it identifies its own
   lines.

Note for whoever picks this up: fact (8) says the tier envs are "subagent plumbing only". That is a
constraint on what the mapping is FOR, not a suggestion — the tiers exist so dispatched subagents
land on the right model, not so the human types a tier name.
acceptance_criteria: Four answers recorded with reasons: shell-function install location mechanism, supported shells, whether the model-to-tier mapping is config or code, and uninstall ownership. No concrete machine path appears in any proposed source file. The answer is consistent with whatever the grilling ticket decided about ccx being in scope — if ccx is out of scope, this issue is closed as not-applicable with that reason.

title: decision: the auto permission classifier's ~40k-per-decision cost — in scope, documented, or ignored
description:
DECISION TICKET. Settled fact (9) on the parent, recorded without a scope decision:

  "auto permission classifier = separate Sonnet-5-tier call through same base URL (~40k input/
  decision — quota cost)"

Read what that measures. When Claude Code runs in auto-permission mode against the router, each
permission decision costs a separate model call carrying roughly 40k input tokens. Through a
metered provider that is a per-decision bill, and a long session makes many decisions.

What must be decided:

1. In scope for qsm-ccr at all?
   The classifier is Claude Code behaviour, not router behaviour. qsm-ccr may have nothing to do
   with it beyond warning that it exists. Decide whether the tool touches it, documents it, or
   ignores it.

2. If documented — where does the warning belong so it is read before the bill arrives?
   Candidates: tools/qsm-ccr/USAGE.md (a reader pulls it on demand, so it may be read too late), or
   the doctor output (read at setup time, which is when the decision is made).

3. Is there a cheaper routing for it?
   The classifier call goes through the same base URL as everything else, so it lands on whatever
   the default model is. Fact (7) lists gpt-5.4-mini at 256k context as the cheapest model on
   codex-api. Whether the classifier CAN be pointed at a cheaper model is unverified — it was
   observed, not tested. Decide whether to test it, and record the answer either way.

Priority is low because nothing is blocked on it: the tool ships without an answer, the user simply
does not learn the cost until they see it. It is filed because "measured once, never written down"
is how a known cost becomes a surprise six months later.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded on this issue: whether qsm-ccr touches, documents, or ignores the classifier; if documented, which surface carries the warning and why that surface is read in time; and whether pointing the classifier at a cheaper model was tested, with the result either way. An untested claim is labelled unverified, never stated as fact.

comments.text: Numeric research: Carbon spacing overview documents 2/4/8 multiples as its own scale; KDE layout_and_nav uses smallSpacing/largeSpacing and an 18px gridUnit. Modular Scale _vars.scss (3.x, line 19) names 1.125 as major-second, one selectable ratio; USWDS font-size tokens are a non-geometric scale. Neither supports imposing 4/8 or 1.125 on every product. NN/g Response Times: The 3 Important Limits supports about 100ms for direct-response feedback, distinct from waiting indicators. NN/g Proximity supports relative grouping but no 1.5x or 3x cutoff; WCAG 1.4.11 uses 3:1 for required visual cues and no 1.5 decoration classification. Use project scales as the expected column, remove unsupported universal cutoffs, retain sourced 100ms. Sources: https://carbondesignsystem.com/elements/spacing/overview/ ; https://develop.kde.org/hig/layout/ ; https://github.com/modularscale/modularscale-sass/blob/3.x/stylesheets/modularscale/_vars.scss ; https://designsystem.digital.gov/design-tokens/typesetting/font-size/ ; https://www.nngroup.com/articles/response-times-3-important-limits/ ; https://www.nngroup.com/articles/gestalt-proximity/ ; https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html .

title: qsm-web: browser reverse-image search for agents
description:
Agents need to submit an image through the web CLI and inspect the resulting source pages, similar images and descriptions without a paid search API. Reuse browserbox instead of building another browser stack. A one-image feasibility assessment has already produced reverse-search results through Google Lens, Yandex and Baidu; the tested Bing flow remains inconclusive.

## Before and after
Today agents can navigate pages and extract text, but the shipped browserbox CLI cannot upload a local file or provide a complete reverse-image workflow. After this change an agent can give a local image or public image URL, select a supported provider, and receive a result or an explicit blocker with browser artifacts.

## Agreed scope
- Providers: Google Lens, Yandex, Baidu and Bing. Preserve Bing's image-description value separately from source matches.
- Exclude Sogou. TinEye, Shutterstock and Lenso are outside the initial automated path.
- Reuse browserbox sessions and allow explicit retention of result tabs for inspection.
- No CAPTCHA bypass, automatic account creation, paid API requirement or image identification by faces.

## Done when
- A local file or public image URL can be submitted through a documented CLI contract for each selected provider; missing input fails before submission.
- The result identifies the provider, actual final URL, outcome, browser instance/tab and requested HTML/screenshot artifacts. A loaded homepage is not success.
- Source matches, visually similar images and generated descriptions are distinguishable. A summary is not presented as provenance evidence.
- A blocked, timed-out, empty or unsupported flow is reported without silently substituting another provider.
- Retained sessions stay available when explicitly requested. Otherwise owned tabs/containers and temporary input copies are cleaned up, leaving the original unchanged.
- A final end-to-end acceptance task exercises the shipped CLI, not only a private diagnostic script.

## Not in this epic
SearXNG server configuration, keyword-search profiles, general browser scraping expansion, paid search integrations, or private infrastructure work.

## Scheduling
Deferred by owner request. Resume after higher-priority private infrastructure security and password-manager work, or when the owner explicitly reprioritizes it. Implementation tasks are created with their specs when planning resumes.

<details><summary>Background</summary>
Completed research and authorized live feasibility assessment: qsm-sarw. The private scratch scripts are evidence, not shipped implementation. Prosopo block detection is separately tracked in qsm-i1u.81 and is not a prerequisite for the initial provider set.
</details>

title: qsm-web: establish a useful Bing image-search browser flow
description:
The owner wants Bing retained because its image descriptions can be useful. The existing assessment accepted an uploaded image but returned a generic text search about Visual Search, not verified image-specific reverse results. Determine the native browser flow before promising Bing support.

## Done when
- An authorized non-sensitive image produces image-specific matches or an image-specific description through a documented sequence, with final HTML/screenshot evidence.
- A generic text SERP is not counted as a working image result.
- If the browser flow is blocked or unavailable, the cause is recorded explicitly and the owner decides the treatment before implementation.
- Descriptions remain separate from exact/source matches.

## Not in this task
Shipping a CLI adapter, bypassing challenges, signing in, paid APIs or changing the provider shortlist.

This is a bounded decision task, not an implementation task. Deferred with the parent epic.

title: qsm-web: test reverse-image search through the installed CLI
description:
Exercise the completed reverse-image feature the way an agent uses it. This is the final acceptance task for the parent epic, not permission to implement or run a new test suite now.

## Done when
- The installed CLI processes a local non-sensitive fixture and a public image URL for the agreed provider set and returns provider-attributed results or explicit observed blockers.
- Returned result URLs and requested HTML/screenshots correspond to actual image-result pages, not homepages or generic text searches.
- Summaries, visual similarity and source matches remain distinguishable.
- Invalid input, provider failure and challenge paths do not silently search another provider.
- Explicitly retained tabs remain inspectable; non-retained owned resources and temporary input copies are cleaned up, with the original file unchanged.
- Every parent acceptance criterion has observed evidence; unavailable cases remain open rather than claimed as passing.

Add dependencies on all implementation tasks when they are created with their specs. Deferred with the parent epic.

title: User feedback: unrequested abstraction — one table rebuilt five times before it was right
description:
Source: Orfeus.Persons ATH-1644 session, 2026-09-01. One RabbitMQ queue-cleanup list was
restructured FIVE times. Every restructure was the user tearing out a layer the model had added
without being asked, and every layer had been defended in prose before being removed.

WHAT THE USER ACTUALLY ASKED FOR, unchanged from the start:
  "the function gets a list of queues, and for each you say whether to keep the data or not, in the
   end they all get deleted, easy. What are you overcomplicating?"

WHAT THE MODEL BUILT INSTEAD, in order, each removed by the user:
  1. `KeepData` set per GROUP in a generator, not per queue. User: "where is the per-queue info?
     What if I wanted PidChange to keep data but OperationResult not?"
  2. `queue with { KeepData = false }` overriding the declared per-item value in code. User:
     "nothing should be overridden, the per-queue setting IS the setting."
  3. `QueueStatus { Live, Retired }` enum, invented so one table could answer two questions. The
     second question ("what does Wolverine listen on?") already had a source the model had itself
     flagged as duplicated a day earlier and then ignored.
  4. `HasLegacySidecarDelayQueues` flag, so a generator could guess names that should have been
     written out.
  5. Flat table with context as a column, written AFTER the user had said the switch was better.
     User: "NENENENEN, the switch was better."
  6. Required `Reason` field, defended twice as auditability. User: "log that you are deleting
     queue X. I don't need a reason."

RESULT AFTER THE USER'S VERSION WON: two files went 475 -> 335 lines, six members deleted, all
1261 tests still green. The simpler design was also the CORRECT one — the layered version had a
data-loss bug the flat one cannot express.

THE USER'S SUMMARY: "you are adding terrible mess there, really terrible."

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS SESSION: the model's own instruction file opens with "Fight complexity"
and "Every addition needs a reason or a showcase that proves the lack." Six additions, zero
showcases. Each was justified by an imagined future requirement, not a demonstrated present one.

Candidate rule material for the marketplace instruction set.
acceptance_criteria:
The pattern is stated as a rule the model can apply mid-task, not just described.
The rule distinguishes 'the user asked for a knob' from 'I imagined a knob would be wanted'.
The rule names the tell: defending a structure in prose before anyone has questioned it.

title: A structure invented so one table can answer two questions
description:
`QueueStatus { Live, Retired }` existed only so a single table could say both 'this is mine and
running' and 'I stopped declaring this'. The second fact already had an owner —
`WolverineExtensions.PidQueuesByContext` — which the model had itself identified as duplicated
earlier in the same session and then quietly rebuilt a second copy of.

The user's question was the fix: "why would it need a second list? The function gets a list of
queues... easy." Deleting the enum and reading the existing source removed the enum, the record it
lived on, a helper, and a whole test.

TELL: a field that exists to disambiguate two meanings inside one container usually means the
container is serving two callers who should each have their own input.
acceptance_criteria:
Rule states: before adding a discriminator field, name the two questions and check whether the
second already has a source in the codebase.

title: Fabricated rows presented as a verified inventory
description:
The model wrote a table documented as 'exactly as it appears on the broker, readable line by line
against the broker's own queue list' and filled 21 of its rows with queue names that have never
existed on any broker: `Delay.First/Next.PersonsService.<NC>.Pid.*` and `DLQ.*.ManualReview`.

The user caught it from a screenshot: "in RabbitMQ these queues do NOT have the context in their
name, you put it there."

Verification the model should have run BEFORE writing the rows, and ran only after being told:
`git log` over every revision of the Sidecar bus config — a PID queue appears in NONE of the seven.
So Sidecar never built a retry-delay pair for one, and ManualReview never had a listener so
Wolverine never gave it a dead-letter queue.

Worse: the model had twice ASSERTED to the user that those queues were 'leftovers from before the
ATH-658 migration'. They were never created at all. A claim inherited from an old code comment was
repeated as established fact, and a bead plus a documentation paragraph were built on it.

TELL: describing an artefact as 'the literal inventory' while any row in it is inferred rather than
observed.
acceptance_criteria:
Rule states: a table documented as an inventory of a live system must have every row observed,
and the observation named. An inferred row is either verified or left out.
Rule states: a fact read from a code comment is a lead, not evidence.

title: Arguing from a fragment the user was never shown
description:
Twice the user said 'I still don't see X in the list' about rows that were present. Both times the
model had pasted only one arm of a three-arm switch into the chat and then reasoned about the whole.
The second time the model started rewriting the structure before checking the file, and only then
found the rows at lines 172-175.

Cost: one unnecessary restructure, and a user reasonably concluding the code was wrong.

TELL: answering 'is X in there?' from memory of what was written rather than from the file.
acceptance_criteria:
Rule states: when the user reports something missing, read the file before agreeing or rewriting.
Rule states: when showing a repetitive structure, show enough that the user can see what is NOT in
the part shown, or say explicitly what was elided.

title: The user's evidence outperformed the model's reasoning three times
description:
Not a failure to fix — a signal about where to spend effort. Three of the session's most valuable
findings came from the user pasting a screenshot or a log, and each overturned something the model
had asserted:

1. A production log line showed the delete had never worked, on any broker, because quorum queues
   refuse a conditional delete outright. The model had reasoned about which of two failure modes it
   was and both guesses were wrong.
2. A broker screenshot showed the ManualReview queues held zero messages. The model had told the
   user twice they were 'permanently non-empty', from an old comment.
3. A broker screenshot showed which queue names really exist, exposing the fabricated rows above.

An external review agent also reproduced a real data-loss bug against a live broker that no amount
of reading had surfaced.

TELL: a claim about the state of a running system that has not been read from that system.
acceptance_criteria:
Rule states: for any claim about a live system's state, either measure it or label it as an
assumption in the same sentence.

title: learn stage: CLOSE lessons check, project skills in .claude/skills, insights due every 50 sessions
description:
Intent (the person, 2026-10-22): adopt the learn stage proposals: a CLOSE check, project-specialized skills, and insights every ~50 sessions; and "jak by fungoval ten automatic qsm usage insights?".

What:
1. CLOSE check: an epic does not close until its lessons are written to their owner (rule, skill plus eval case, AGENTS.md, project skill, feedback task, spec design or commit) or the close says none were found.
2. Project skills: a skill for one project lives in that repo's .claude/skills/, held to the marketplace bar (12 KB cap, a description that fires, an eval); it moves into a marketplace plugin when a second project needs it. Write the convention into qsm-builder add-skill and the instructions.
3. Insights cadence: qsm-usage counts sessions since the last insights run in its ledger; at session start, once 50 new sessions exist, the brief says insights are due; the main agent runs the insights pipeline (haiku facets, synthesis) and proposes rules; nothing is written without the person's yes. No unattended run: it costs model calls and every result needs confirmation.

Acceptance: a closed epic shows its lessons line; one project skill exists in a repo under the convention and passes its eval; after 50 sessions a live session's brief names insights as due, and the run writes nothing before the person confirms.

title: qsm-langdev-qml: a langdev module for QML, Quickshell and desktop UI/UX
description: Intent: the owner asked for it after the qsm-shell and qsm-desktop night run ("musime udelat qml/quickshell/desktop/ui/ux langdev module/s"). Today QML work has no langdev module: qmllint runs through each repo's own scripts, nothing gates a commit on QML, and the measured QML and Quickshell platform facts and component laws live only in the two AGENTS.md files. What it should hold (to be grilled before building): the commit and push gates for .qml (qmllint with the Qt 6 and Quickshell import paths, qmlformat, the repo's baseline the way the other langdev modules diff against HEAD), the authoring skill (the platform facts both AGENTS.md list: hot reload versus fresh start, inline components, Screen vs window devicePixelRatio, Flickable contentItem, WheelHandler under Wayland, defaulted typed parameters, on<Capital> properties), and the hook into the UI validation instruments (qsm-compuse drive: slot shell, whole-surface check, merge gate, qsm-j480.13) so a UI change is gated by measurement, not lint alone. Open: one module or two (QML/Quickshell code vs desktop UI/UX checks); where qsm-uix's qml-ui and desktop-ui skills end and this begins.

title: marketplace: out-of-loop rule: build what is approved, merge after review, end in a report
description:
Decision (the person, 2026-10-22, answering the outloop question): "Vše schválené": when the person is away, an agent may build anything whose intent and spec the person already approved, plus bugs and feedback that have a task. This replaces the 2026-10-19 decision (session ba1413e4 #128-#132) that a night run only plans and triages.

What: write the rule into plugins/qsm-setup/instructions (context rule or CLAUDE.md loop): out of loop, work only from an approved intent and spec or a task; every change in a worktree; strict review per batch (one reviewer per four branches); merge only what passes the gates and review; product choices are never guessed but collected; the run ends with a report and the batch of decisions; the lessons pass waits for the person's confirmation.

Acceptance: the generated rule holds it; validate passes; the next night run follows it.

title: Feedback: every finding about the marketplace, one place, source as a label

title: qsm-forge: gl threads fails with 'unexpected shape' on a merge request whose discussions hold system notes
description:
reporter: main agent, session 2026-10-29
what: 'qsm-forge gl threads 82' and 'gl status' both failed: 'glab api .../discussions?per_page=100&page=1 answered with an unexpected shape' and printed the first discussion, an individual_note system note ('assigned to a colleague', type null). The parser rejects the whole page instead of skipping system notes.
how: every MR with an assignment or label change has such notes, so threads is unusable on real MRs; the hook also blocks the raw glab api read, so there was no way to list what the failed submit-review had posted except 'glab mr view --comments'.
why: threads is the handle for every reply; fix: accept notes with type null and system true and skip them.

title: qsm-setup: context rule sent review to haiku; the person wants review on opus, implementation on sonnet, haiku only for basic work
description:
reporter: main agent, recording the user (2026-10-29, ATH-1847 session)
what: rules/context.md 'Who does what' table put review, audit and verify under haiku and made every workflow step haiku. The user's own ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md says sonnet is the default subagent and haiku is for runners and swarms; the generated rule contradicted it and the main agent followed the generated rule.
user's words: 'proc haiku? proc ne sonnet? ... V models ma byt napsane ze takova basic prace je pro haiku, ale review a tezsi implementace je sonnet nebo opus, review spise opus.'
how: a strict review of two MR branches (!188, !184 in Orfeus.Persons) was dispatched on haiku.
why: a review on a model that plans less far ahead misses the seams; the person pays a round trip with a colleague.
fix: table rewritten in plugins/qsm-setup/instructions/rules/context.md (haiku = basic work, sonnet = implementation, opus = review), workflow paragraph aligned, regenerated with qsm-setup activate.
close_reason: Decided 2026-10-30 by the person: keep sonnet as the default review tier and opus for a large or risky change; the table already says a review is never haiku, which was the defect.

title: marketplace: wt merge fast-forwards main without running hooks/post-merge, so bins stay old
description: Seen 2026-10-30 (session 6c7fc7b0): after 'wt merge main --no-squash' of pack-idle-transcripts moved main to 7862d74f, refresh.log had no entry for it and the installed qsm-memory still said 'unknown verb pack'; running 'bash hooks/post-merge' in the main checkout by hand rebuilt it. title: qsm-ccr: the daemon start test fails once under a full parallel suite
description: Seen 2026-10-30 (session 6c7fc7b0) by the implementer of pack-idle-transcripts: 'a start or a reload proves the daemon down > a start that never opens the port is taken down and failed' in plugins/qsm-ccr/scripts/cli.test.ts failed once in 'bun test ./ ./.gates' (2098 pass, 1 fail) and passed alone (63/0) and in two later full runs. Likely a timing limit as tight as the expected time under load; unverified. Done when the full suite passes it under load, or the cause is named.

title: qsm-setup: the main agent recommended --instructions append against the person's rule that the plugin is the source
description: what: after moving the instructions to qsm-setup, the main agent told the person to run activate with append, and the setup skill, README, USAGE and spec said append is the default and to ask before an overwrite. how: the person's rule is that everything is written in the plugin and propagated by overwrite; only device or system specific text lives directly in the config, so append is an exception. Fixed in the same session: overwrite is the default in the skill, README, USAGE, spec and the option's description. why: append kept a stale qsm-adapter block and a second copy of the instructions.
close_reason: append mode is gone: qsm-setup activate has only --instructions replace; no source mentions append (checked 2026-10-14)

title: marketplace: main agent dispatched three implementers into its own tree instead of making their worktrees
description: what: the main agent gave three parallel implementers the path of the rewrite worktree; all three edited and committed there. One commit swept another agent's files (reset by the agent), and a staged file of the main agent landed in a subagent's commit (split afterwards). how: the context rule says the main agent makes a subagent's worktree before dispatch; the prompt said 'your own worktree' but named the shared path. why: one agent, one tree (AGENTS.md).
close_reason: Fixed on main in 35c07567 (night batch, reviewed, full gates green: 1806 tests, test:hooks 108).

title: qsm-memory: agent dumped whole sessions with show instead of search and windowed reads
description: what: asked what happened on rewrite in recent sessions, the main agent called the MCP show on whole sessions. One (106k chars) was refused by the harness and saved to a file; one (46 turns, f49cc5fa) landed whole in the main context. The user: 'Proc si hned dostal fing 100k tokens into context on load?' how: list, then search for the topic, then show with lines a-b on the decisive turns, or the recall agent for a broad summary. why: the context rule says output over about 20 lines goes to a file or a subagent; show has no size cap and no summary mode, so nothing stops a whole-session dump.
close_reason: 674bf1d7+e45a7975: show stops at 20 000 characters with next: --lines; the real 46-turn session went from 53 687 to about 20 400 characters

title: marketplace: branches and worktrees are left unmerged behind finished work
description: what: on 2026-10-11 the repo held 17 branches besides rewrite and main: 11 merged agent-* branches and feat/t1fx-3-function-hooks (deleted now), and 6 unmerged: web-slice with its worktree (10 commits, main agent of session f49cc5fa, left waiting on a push decision), agent-a36493da8a5fc3072 and backup/ledger-ignore (8 each, langdev ledger), agent-a3961d05b8fe2e0b1 (4, statusline test titles), chore/opencode-strip-contract-hooks (14, 7 weeks, checked out in the main checkout), feat/qsm-searxng-params (1, 3 months). The person: 'To by se nikdy nemelo stat, subagents si vytvari subbranches aby mohli pracovat parallel, az to dodelaji, tak vsechno musi jit vzdycky zpatky do current working branch. Takze budto ten worktree smaz, a nebo si ho prevezmi.' how: the context rule covers a subagent's worktree only; extend it so any branch an agent opens, its own included, is merged back into the working branch or deleted before the turn that finished it ends, and the session-end hook (worktrunk) names every branch ahead of the working branch. why: an unmerged branch is finished work the working tree does not have; this session nearly merged a vertical-slice model the person had already replaced.

title: qsm-essentials: two runners of one command write one log file
description: what: two runner agents started in parallel for sleep 20 both wrote scratchpad/runner.sleep.1.log, so the second overwrote the first; told to run in /tmp, a sonnet runner also wrote its log to /tmp instead of the scratchpad. how: name the log by the agent's own id or a timestamp, and keep the log in the scratchpad whatever the command's directory. why: a briefing points at a log that holds another run, or leaves a file outside the scratchpad.

title: marketplace: bun run lint fails on rewrite
description: what: bun run lint on rewrite (b6c0d126) reports 9 findings outside the cockpit: qsm-langdev 3 (compare.test.ts, cli.test.ts lines per function), qsm-usage 3, qsm-uix 2 (capture.ts noIncrementDecrement, errors.ts noExcessiveClassesPerFile), qsm-statusline 1 (git.ts cognitive complexity). how: fix each or narrow the rule with a reason in biome.jsonc. why: the commit gate counts on lint, and a red gate hides a new finding.
close_reason: Fixed on main: Biome was replaced by oxlint and oxfmt; bun run lint on main passes clean (476 files, 2026-10-19).

title: qsm-usage: the output filter rewrites commands whose output goes to a file
description: what: the qsm-usage tool.call hook hands every Bash command to rtk hook claude, which rewrites head -211 f.tsx > out.tsx into rtk read f.tsx --max-lines 211 > out.tsx; rtk read writes 142 summarised lines with elided bodies and '[N more lines]' into the file instead of 211 lines. This corrupted plugins' register.tsx once in session 2eb0df0a. It also rewrites find . -newermt '-10 minutes' into rtk find, which prints a count summary instead of the matching files, and grep into rtk grep ('3 matches in 3 files'). Agents then route around it with /usr/bin/grep and /usr/bin/find. how: never filter a command that redirects stdout to a file or pipes into another command, and leave find with predicates rtk does not support unrewritten; a test that runs head -N file > out through the hook and compares bytes. why: a filter that saves tokens must never change data a command writes, and a silent rewrite of find makes a correct command lie.
close_reason: Fixed on main in 35c07567 (night batch, reviewed, full gates green: 1806 tests, test:hooks 108).

title: qsm-langdev: the result store serves a stale tsc and depcruise result after bun install
description: what: in the main checkout, check --against origin/main reported tsc 13->21 and depcruise 18->7 on lib/mcp-stdio.ts and the qsm-index/qsm-memory mcp files; after bun install the same check still said 'shipped hit' with the same WORSE lines; deleting .qsm-langdev/results/{tsc,depcruise} made it pass. how: the store key holds the tree, not the installed dependencies, so a result scored without node_modules is reused once they exist. why: a gate that blocks on a stale cached result sends the person after a regression that is not there.
close_reason: result key hashes installed package names and lockfiles for tsc, depcruise, knip (335642e5, d8bd9989)

title: qsm-langdev: pre-commit blocks a markdown-only commit in an agent worktree
description: reporter: qsm-ccr spec subagent. what: the qsm-langdev pre-commit gate blocks a commit that only adds two markdown files (plugins/qsm-ccr README and spec) in an agent worktree. how: (1) no config profile is recorded for this repository, and the suggested qsm-langdev init --profile general fails with unknown profile general (known: none); (2) sentrux-gate reports quality 7515 to 7487, worse by 28, with 0 cross-module edges added, for markdown only; QSM_LANGDEV_ALLOW did not pass either block. why: an agent cannot commit a spec-only change from a worktree, and the gate's own remediation command fails.

title: marketplace: qsm-secrets guard crashes on assignment-only commands; function-hook review
description:
# Review: qsm-secrets guard crash and function-hook findings

Source: workflow wf_257c23d7-e15. Full returns: /home/qs_m4rk/.claude/projects/-home-qs-m4rk/f58473c1-6c01-4751-be7e-34e7ef1cb666/subagents/workflows/wf_257c23d7-e15/journal.jsonl
Facts are measured unless marked inferred or unverified.

## Summary

- One defect blocks calls today: the guard crashes on assignment-only commands. Reproduced.
- Four hook sites call next(e) again inside a catch without next.called. They can wait.
- Count of the 69 candidates: 11 real, 15 unknown, 43 noise. The review text said 17 unknown and 41 noise; a recount from the journal gives 15 and 43.

## 1. Fix now: guard crashes on assignment-only statements

- Where: plugins/qsm-secrets/lib/guard.ts:503 (followCd) and :542 (heredoc interpreter check).
- Code: `wordToLit(call.args[0] as Word)`. args is empty for `NAME=value` or `NAME=$(cmd)`. The `?? ""` does not catch a throw inside wordToLit.
- Repro on the installed bin ~/.local/bin/qsm-secrets (built from 733c9536): `echo a` passes; `p=1; echo a` and `p=$(date)` fail with "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'w.parts')", exit 1.
- Effect: fail-closed. Every Bash call with such a statement is denied, except the exact `qsm-secrets doctor` line (hooks/register.tsx:102).
- Fix: return early when call.args.length === 0 at both sites. Remove the `as Word` casts.
- Tests: add `p=1; echo a`, `p=$(date)` and `A=1` to the guard cases in scripts/cli.test.ts. They must fail before the fix. The current guard cases have no assignment-only statement, so they pass with the bug.
- Open: not every crash in this session had an assignment. `git archive <ref> | tar -x -C <dir>` failed 4 of 4 times for one agent. Not explained.

## 2. A reinstall alone does not fix it

- The live hook runs the compiled bin, built from 733c9536, which has the bug. Reinstalling from 733c9536 installs the same bug.
- Plugin cache 0.1.0 (gitCommitSha 2b7c1bed, installed 2026-10-04) is stale: it has blocked.ts and no guard.ts. It is not what runs.
- known_marketplaces.json: qsm-marketplace is a directory source at .claude/worktrees/rewrite (HEAD 733c9536). Removing that worktree after the merge would remove the source. How the harness reacts to a missing source is unverified.
- Order: fix, tests, rebuild the bin, replace the bin, repoint the marketplace, reinstall, control.

## 3. Control: proposed pass criteria

1. The new test cases fail at 733c9536 and pass after the fix.
2. `printf 'p=1; echo a\n' | qsm-secrets guard --json` returns code ok and denied false, from the rebuilt bin.
3. A real Bash tool call that starts with `x=1;` runs.
4. Existing refusal cases still refuse (vault-reader and the others).

## 4. Function hooks: real, can wait

| Site | Why | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| qsm-usage hooks/register.tsx:327 (carryOn), :382 (registerToon) | next(e) is awaited at 369; a later throw sends carryOn to call next(e) again. A Bash write could run twice. | inferred |
| qsm-worktrunk hooks/register.tsx:55 | the catch calls next(e) without next.called; a downstream throw may run the chain twice | inferred |
| qsm-langdev hooks/register.tsx:61-64 (registerEditFindings) | next(e) is awaited at 48, then $.langdev.edited may throw; the catch calls next(e) again. An Edit could apply twice. | inferred |

Fix pattern: qsm-secrets hooks/register.tsx:299 already checks next.called. How the engine behaves on a second next() is unverified.

## 5. Unknown (15): one engine probe would settle most

- qsm-cockpit hooks/register.tsx:79, 103, 198, 204, 254, 448: no .catch (session.start, stage tool.call, turn.start, turn.complete, AbovePrompt render, Pane render). qsm-usage paneText catches and shows an ERROR line; compare.
- qsm-memory hooks/register.tsx:62: session.compact has no .catch.
- qsm-usage hooks/register.tsx:156, 300, 304: an unchecked read; breakdown and ledger tool.call handlers have no try/catch.
- qsm-langdev hooks/register.tsx:13: failed() slices error.message ?? error.kind; safe only if Caught has one of them.
- lib/guard.ts:428 and :447: does the parser always emit Redirect.word (heredoc, `3>&1`)?
- shell-ast: node_modules is absent in the worktree; the pin is 0.8.0. The version is not the discriminator for the crash.
- Engine questions: what happens to a hook with no .catch, and what a second next() call does. The types are not generated, so both are unverified.

## 6. Typing: why the noise bucket matters

- The guard bug is an `as Word` cast on an array index. TypeScript sees Word, not Word or undefined. The cast hides the hole.
- plugins/qsm-secrets/hooks/tsconfig.json sets strict and noUncheckedIndexedAccess (measured). Its include lists ../lib/blocked.ts, which is deleted on main. Whether guard.ts is type-checked through it is unverified.
- .claude/types is empty, so the engine types (Caught, process.run result, next result) are not checked.
- Next step: generate the types, run tsc -p plugins/qsm-secrets/hooks, and compare its output with the noise list below.

## 7. Noise (43), kept for the record

Judged from the code, without generated types.

- lib/guard.ts: 268, 341, 253, 287, 290, 458, 507, 543, 236, 224, 230, 519, 452, 558 (14)
- shell-ast patched dist check (1)
- qsm-cockpit: 68, 443 (2)
- qsm-essentials: 7, 20 (2)
- qsm-forge: 24 (1)
- qsm-langdev: 32, 41, 50 (3)
- qsm-memory: 65 (1)
- qsm-secrets hooks/register.tsx: 56, 147, 162, 209, 224, 286, 290, 302 (8)
- qsm-setup: 20 (1)
- qsm-usage: 256, 268, 276, 292, 337, 351, 401, 407 (8)
- qsm-worktrunk: 33, 42 (2)

Reasons in short: deliberate fail-closed deny with toast and log (secrets 147, 162, 302; forge 24; langdev 32, 41; worktrunk 33); a value its type says is always set (usage 256, 268, 276, 292); a cast whose reader is guarded elsewhere (guard 341, 458, 507, 543); an unchecked read whose caller catches it (cockpit 68).

## 8. Side findings

- The main checkout /home/qs_m4rk/Projects/FullStack.qsm/qsm-marketplace is on branch langdev-oxc with a dirty tree. Its plugins/qsm-secrets/lib has blocked.ts and no guard.ts.
- The qsm-worktrunk hook blocks `git worktree list`. Use `wt list`.
- Related open task: qsm-i1u.22 (custom hooks and the mod still throw). Check for overlap before work starts.

title: marketplace: the pre-push typecheck gate fails on a red origin/main, so an agent cannot push a docs-only commit
description:
What: pushing ff2deea3 (markdown only, under plugins/qsm-uix) to main ran hooks/pre-push: the qsm-langdev hook, bun run validate, bun run typecheck. typecheck reported 35 tsc errors at origin/main e0e81fcc, the same 35 with and without the commit (plugins/qsm-secrets/lib/guard.ts among them), measured in a scratch worktree after bun install. The hook refuses --no-verify. QSM_LANGDEV_ALLOW="<why>" is written for the person, and the auto-mode classifier denied it when an agent set it. So an agent has no path to push a docs-only commit while main is red; the commit waits on branch uix-skills.
Why: one red commit on main freezes every push by every agent until a person types the bypass, whatever the pushed change touches.
How: the typecheck step of the gate compares against the push base (origin/<branch>) and fails only on errors the pushed range adds, naming them; or the gate skips typecheck when the pushed range touches no .ts and no tsconfig; and main gets green first (qsm-i1u.26 holds the stale-result side of the same gate).
Done when: a markdown-only commit on top of a red origin/main pushes with no bypass, and the gate's message names which errors are new to the range.
close_reason: decided 2026-10-22: pre-push keeps blocking on a red origin/main; a red main is fixed, not bypassed

title: marketplace: the eval runner refuses a whole plugin when one unselected case has a broken regex grader

What: bun run eval qsm-uix --case ui-design-monochrome-shell exited 1 with "regex graders broken, no model was run: unrelated-coding-negative ... samples/pass.md is missing". .gates/plugin-eval.ts:232 runs brokenGraders(all) over every case before the --case filter applies. Done when: bun run eval <plugin> --case X runs with another case's grader broken, and the warning names that case.

title: marketplace: haiku judges in scenario evals failed correct replies; regex on planted vocabulary measured the delta
description:
What: in qsm-uix ui-design-monochrome-shell the LLM grader "fix-is-a-structure-with-one-separation" got judge votes FAIL FAIL FAIL on with-runs whose reply did what the skill says (kept the violet tint on the neutrals, one separation mechanism); a first shared-hue regex passed both arms, so it measured nothing. The ui-audit three-mechanisms LLM grader flipped the same way. The graders that separated the arms (3/3 with, 0/3 without) are regexes on vocabulary the skill plants: "separation mechanism", the "15 degrees" hue limit, the 1.3:1 ratio. Five runs were needed (scratchpad eval-uix.log to eval-uix-5.log, this session).
Why: a scenario eval written with haiku judges costs runs and can fail a correct skill, so the bar reads as a skill defect when it is a grader defect.
How: the eval guidance (plugins/qsm-builder/skills/skill-standards/SKILL.md and the header of .gates/plugin-eval.ts) says: a scenario grader is a regex on a word or number the skill plants and an unaided model would not say; an LLM grader only for what no regex can see, with a rubric that quotes the skill's sentence; a grader that passes both arms is deleted. qsm-uix's two scenarios are the instance.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Main-agent follow-up: qsm-web browserbox start timed out at 60 s, but bbox-11000 became resident and daemon ready. Both qsm-web browserbox fetch and script fail because lib/browserbox.ts sends stdin JSON to /opt/driver/ctl.py, while the installed image ctl.py requires positional arguments. Inspected runtime ctl.py directly. Verified read-only command docker exec bbox-11000 /opt/venv/bin/python /opt/driver/ctl.py fetch https://www.reddit.com/ --screenshot --keep --settle 3000 --timeout 30000 --out /out returned ok:true, blocked:false, HTTP 200, title Reddit, tab 1. This is a wrapper/image protocol mismatch, not proven Reddit blocking. Passed exact working interface and exclusive bbox-11000 ownership to community researcher; no shared source or config edited. nlm list separately attempted automatic login and timed out with unknown PrivateNetworkRequestPolicy PermissionBlock, so no notebook was created.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Main supplied a verified runtime path: existing /opt/driver/ctl.py accepts positional commands while qsm wrapper sends stdin JSON. On delegated exclusive bbox-11000, docker exec bbox-11000 /opt/venv/bin/python /opt/driver/ctl.py fetch <public Reddit thread> --screenshot --keep --settle 3000 --timeout 30000 --out /out succeeded with HTTP 200, blocked:false. I read ctl.py command construction and used its extract <tab> --selector body --text contract. Thus the research can proceed through the inspected runtime without a login. The wrapper failure is not evidence Reddit is blocked in the real browser.

title: qsm-uix: qml-ui skill lacks the on<Capital> property-name law
description: What: the qml-ui skill does not warn that a QML property named on<Capital> (onPrimary) is read as a signal-handler name. How it bit: Theme.qml declared property color onPrimary with a Behavior on it inside a pragma Singleton; Quickshell 0.3.2 / Qt 6.12 segfaulted at load with no QML error, the supervisor crash-looped and the owner's desktop was down for over an hour (2026-10-16, qsm-desktop commit 20303e1). Why a skill rule: the design system names the role on-primary, so every port from a token file into QML will reach for onPrimary; one line in qml-ui (never name a property on followed by a capital letter; use textOnPrimary) prevents the crash. The library AGENTS.md of qsm-shell now holds the law locally.

title: qsm-web browserbox: start keeps a stale image whose driver speaks an older protocol, so every start fails with 'browser never answered'
description: What: qsm-web browserbox start failed with 'bbox-11000 started but its browser never answered; nothing was left running' in this session and for two subagents. Cause, measured: the local image qsm-browserbox was built 2026-07-20 and its /opt/driver/ctl.py takes argv ('usage: ctl.py <cmd> ...'), while the current client sends one JSON job on stdin (plugins/qsm-web/docker/driver/ctl.py reads sys.stdin, since 5fff6b01). ensureImage in scripts/browserbox.ts builds only when the image is missing, so a stale image is never replaced and the ping never succeeds. Fixed here by hand: docker build --tag qsm-browserbox plugins/qsm-web/docker; start and a reddit fetch then worked. Fix: tag the image with a hash of plugins/qsm-web/docker (or a label) and rebuild when it differs, or have install rebuild it; name the mismatch in the error instead of 'never answered'. title: qsm-secrets: fake-shell CLI conformance tests intermittently exceed the test deadline
description: Discovered while validating the qsm-web targeted reconstruction. With unchanged qsm-secrets code and Bun1.4.3, full repository runs intermittently time out at the default5s on different fake-backend CLI cases: rbw/set/empty prompt baseline7112ms, rbw/get/no-fd3 in implementer run, libsecret/get/no-fd3 in final sequential main run5076ms. Evidence /tmp/opencode/qsm-web-production-baseline-repo-tests.log, /tmp/opencode/qsm-web-final-tests.log, /tmp/opencode/qsm-web-secrets-rate-*.log. comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: New decisive environment evidence: under mise exec -- bun, process.execPath is the pinned Bun1.4.3 actual binary, but Bun.which("bun") resolves /home/qs_m4rk/.local/share/vite-plus/bin/bun. Tests that spawn bare bun with isolated HOME therefore run a different dispatcher than the parent, explaining why direct process.execPath tests pass while bare-runtime conformance cases stall/fail. Latest run had33 cascading failures across multiple plugins, not a qsm-secrets-only defect. Next controlled input: prepend dirname(process.execPath) only in this command environment, preserve pinned Bun and unchanged tests/deadlines, compare same suite. Do not edit personal PATH or suite timeouts.

comments.text: Controlled symptom movement confirms runtime mismatch: without code/test/deadline changes, set only per-command PATH to dirname(mise which bun) before the same full-suite command. Both process.execPath and Bun.which("bun") then resolve the pinned Bun1.4.3 binary, and the full suite passes1817/1817 with0 failures in161.50s. Prior mismatched Vite+ dispatcher run had1785 pass/33 fail plus a temp leak. No personal shell config changed. Keep this finding open for durable test/runtime selection cleanup: direct process.execPath or consistent pinned PATH, not timeout increases.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Later qsm-qjr lifecycle verification found a concrete runtime-selection hazard: pinning the parent with mise exec was insufficient when child tests called bare bun, because PATH selected /home/qs_m4rk/.local/share/vite-plus/bin/bun instead of mise Bun1.4.3. Command-scoped PATH prefix from dirname(mise which bun) fixed the later whole suite unchanged (1832 ordinary+108hooks green). title: qsm-compuse: drive move overshoots onto the neighbouring monitor when the target is within 40px of an edge shared with it
description: What: drive move steps 60% of the remaining delta per ydotool relative move and the compositor's pointer acceleration multiplies it. From (768,432) to (30,32) on eDP-1 the polled path was (352,207) -> (-6,13) -> (33,33): x went negative, i.e. onto HDMI-A-1 (x -1536..0, left of eDP-1). HDMI-A-1's scene has its own notification bell hot corner at its top-right, so the pass at its local (1532,15) opened the notifications modal on the focused monitor and moved Hyprland focus to HDMI-A-1. Every later capture in the survey then carried an open notification centre, and the pointer was left on the other monitor. How: two monitors side by side, drive move X Y with X < ~100 from the far side of the screen; poll hyprctl cursorpos during the move. Why it matters: a hover survey of a left rail is polluted by a surface the test never asked for, and the owner's second monitor changes focus. Workaround used: approach in two stages (move to x=120, then to x=30). Suggested: clamp the last steps (cap the step by the distance to the nearest monitor edge it must not cross) or finish with warp-then-nudge, and say in USAGE.md that moves near a shared edge need a staged approach. Where discovered: qsm-shell/qsm-desktop unified live validation.

title: qsm-secrets: session.append mask is skipped under cc-plugin-sec-default, substituted secrets reach the transcript unmasked
description:
What: on this account the built-in module cc-plugin-sec-default (switched on because the organization sends remote managed settings) skips user-plugin hooks on some events. On 2026-10-21 the engine reported:

    qsm-secrets: its session.append hook was skipped. "cc-plugin-sec-default" runs first and sent the event on past it.
    qsm-usage: its prompt.attachment hook was skipped. "cc-plugin-sec-default" runs first and sent the event on past it.

Why it matters: registerMask in plugins/qsm-secrets/hooks/register.tsx is the fail-closed mask of every row the conversation keeps. When it is skipped, the output of a command that ran with a substituted secret enters the conversation and the transcript unmasked, while tool.call substitution still runs. The spec promises a mask that never happens on this machine, and nothing but a one-line notice says so. qsm-usage loses prompt.attachment rows in its ledger (same class as the prompt.section and prompt.context loss found 2026-10-09).

How: either find an event the module admits for the mask (tool.result or the session.end scrub), or make the substitution refuse when the mask is known to be skipped, so the state is loud, not silent. Update AGENTS.md / the hook rule with the list of events skipped under sec-default.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Done: qsm-memory reads a compaction from the conversation on prompt.submit (merge 93386c6a); qsm-usage dropped its passed-over prompt.attachment and skill.prompt hooks and reads the conversation at turn.complete (merge 1dc8fa35). Left: qsm-secrets spec must name the attachment, hook-context and compaction rows as unmasked under cc-plugin-sec-default, and the marketplace spec's admitted list (session.compact is passed over).

title: qsm-compuse: a workflow agent captured the live Hyprland with grim and crashed the owner's session (SIGBUS in screencopy)
description: What: at 00:29:29 on 2026-10-22 Hyprland pid 2253 died with SIGBUS (BUS_ADRERR) in Screenshare::CScreenshareFrame::copyShm -> CGLFramebuffer::readPixels, i.e. while copying a frame into a client's shm buffer. The only screencopy client at the time was a desktop-rebuild workflow agent running its own script (scratchpad rebuild/tools2/ntcap.sh: grim -o eDP-1 plus hyprctl focus switches on the owner's monitors) instead of drive slot; its rtk wrapper aborted (SIGABRT) at 00:29:15. The watchdog restarted Hyprland in --safe-mode, and the restarted compositor could not open the NVIDIA GPU because the kernel module (615.71.09, boot 2026-10-10) no longer matched userspace (615.78.08, upgraded 2026-10-12), so the external monitor went dark. How: agent prompts allowed live captures; nothing in drive refused a live-session capture from a subagent. Why it matters: one dead compositor takes every window and the owner's work with it. Fix: subagents capture only in DRIVE_SLOT; drive refuses a live grim/wf-recorder when DRIVE_SLOT is unset and the caller is not the main agent; agent-written capture scripts that call grim or hyprctl dispatch directly are forbidden in workflow prompts.
close_reason: drive refuses every capture and input verb outside a slot unless DRIVE_LIVE=1; slot run strips HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE and DISPLAY; the skill forbids subagents grim, wf-recorder and hyprctl dispatch/reload/eval; a whole shell runs isolated in a slot under dbus-run-session (verified: qsm-desktop renders in a 1920x1080@1.25 slot).

title: qsm-secrets: ask the organization admin to seat qsm-secrets before cc-plugin-sec-default
description:
What: a request to the organization's Claude Code admin, written so the admin can hand it to their own agent. It lets the person's own security and measurement plugins run before the built-in policy module, so they see what that module hides from them today.

Why: the organization sends remote managed settings (~/.claude/remote-settings.json on the person's machine: a command deny list and auto-mode rules). Because managed settings exist, Claude Code seats its built-in module cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin outermost, and for any plugin the person installs it passes over: every classic hook (hooks.json), prompt.section, prompt.context, prompt.attachment, prompt.compose, skill.prompt, attribution.text, session.compact, settings.read, and session.append rows on the doors attachment, hook-context and compaction (measured from the Claude Code 2.1.307 binary and from the "<plugin>: its <event> hook was skipped" notices in every session). Effects today:
- qsm-secrets cannot mask a secret that reaches the conversation inside an attachment, hook context or a compaction summary.
- qsm-usage cannot measure the system prompt sections, CLAUDE.md, attachments and skill text through their own events.
- qsm-memory had to move off session.compact.
The binary's own text: "Security default: seated outermost on a machine with managed settings and for Team and Enterprise organizations unless managed prependPlugins is set, in which case the organization lists cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin there or not". Only plugins enabled by managed settings can be seated by prependPlugins ("not seated: managed prependPlugins does not list it").

What we ask the admin (smallest first):
1. Seat qsm-secrets before the security default, for this one user or the whole org:
   - managed extraKnownMarketplaces: the marketplace github.com/Questi0nM4rk/qsm-marketplace under the name qsm-marketplace;
   - managed enabledPlugins: "qsm-secrets@qsm-marketplace": true;
   - managed prependPlugins: ["qsm-secrets@qsm-marketplace", "cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin"] (keep the security default in the list so the organization's policy still runs, just after the mask).
2. Optional, measurement only: the same for qsm-usage@qsm-marketplace, placed after cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin (appendPlugins or later in prependPlugins), so it reads prompt.section, prompt.context, prompt.attachment and skill.prompt without touching policy.
3. Nothing else: no change to the deny list or auto-mode rules is needed.

Instructions for the admin's agent:
- Open the organization's Claude Code managed settings (the admin console's managed settings for Claude Code, the source of remote-settings.json). Read the current JSON first; change only the keys above; keep every existing key.

title: qsm-secrets: mask --all --json truncates stdout at 64 KiB multiples, the hook then withholds a subagent prompt
description:
reporter: main agent, session 2026-10-29 advisor-authorization review (incident, the user's word)
what: the compiled qsm-secrets binary prints the outcome envelope with process.stdout.write and the process exits right after. On a pipe the write is asynchronous, so the envelope is cut at a buffer boundary and the hook that masks every subagent prompt (plugins/qsm-secrets/hooks/register.tsx maskWalk -> noun.generated.ts unwrap) throws 'printed no envelope' or 'stdout is not an outcome envelope', fails closed and replaces the prompt with 'qsm-secrets: this text could not be masked and was withheld'.
how: measured today with 'qsm-secrets mask --all --json < file':
  33 B input  -> 180 B stdout, complete envelope
  159 KB input -> 73 728 B stdout (exactly 72 KiB), truncated JSON
  477 KB input -> 131 072 B stdout (exactly 128 KiB), truncated JSON
  exit 0, no stderr in every case.
  In the review workflow the Integrate agent's prompt (about 100 KB, the findings of five slice reviewers inline) reached the agent as the withheld notice only; 57 agents ran, the final report was never written. Second run with the findings in a file instead of inline passed.
why: a prompt-sized text is normal in a workflow; a masking step that silently cannot handle it turns a safety hook into a work killer. Fix where it lives: lib/cli-base.ts emit/processIo must await the stdout drain (Bun.write(Bun.stdout, text) returned promise, or set process.exitCode and return instead of process.exit). lib/cli-base.ts is staged by another session right now, so not fixed here. A test: a 200 KB array through mask --all --json comes back whole.
