how: a 3-file commit in plugins/qsm-index was blocked twice. The --no-verify escape is itself blocked by the langdev hook and needs the user to type QSM_LANGDEV_ALLOW by hand.
why: a gate that can never pass is a gate everyone bypasses. Two causes to separate: why semgrep spends 17 s of CPU on --version (python import chain? network version check?), and whether the probe should cache the version it measured once (the store already keys on tool version) instead of re-probing on every commit.

title: qsm-index: search and graph build time out at 25 s on Orfeus.Contract
description:
reporter: main agent (Orfeus.Contract session, 2026-10-27)
what: qsm-index on /home/qsm/Projects/Orfeus/Orfeus.Contract (.NET repo, ~90 MB EF migrations folder) is unusable: every search call stops with 'semble ran past the 25000 ms call limit and was stopped' (3 of 3, with and without a build running); the build fails the same way: 'graphify ran past the 25000 ms call limit and was stopped'. status and context also disagree: status says built at HEAD, 0 files changed; context on the same repo answered 'index is stale; reindex started'.
how: user asked to index and search Contract; status -> present at HEAD; search -> timeout; context -> stale + reindex; reindex finished -> failed again on graphify 25 s.
why: the tool the user asked for cannot answer one query on a work repo, so the agent falls back to grep; the stale/at-HEAD contradiction triggers needless rebuilds. Large generated files (156 *.Designer.cs ~740 KB each) are a likely cause (unverified): consider excluding generated/migration files or raising the per-call limit for builds.
close_reason: Fixed in 4a4b0930 (merge 70821513, pushed). Cause: the detached build used the 25 s MCP call limit; graphify needs 173 s on 111 MB of generated C#. Now: a build has no limit, calls 5 min, qsm-index wait + hooks tell the person (toast) and the agent (next prompt) when a build ends; a refresh in a removed worktree cwd no longer toasts. Proved: cold reindex of a 111 MB repo returns in 0 s, wait prints 'indexed at f38cd9176506 in 266 s'; main's build failed at 25 s on the same repo. The search half was the same cause: search needs the semble cache that the failed build never warmed.

comments.author: qsm
comments.text: 2026-10-29, main agent: root cause found and fixed on branch fix/qsm-index-build-limit (worktree ~/Projects/qsm-marketplace.fix-qsm-index-build-limit, uncommitted: the commit is blocked by the langdev semgrep probe, see qsm-i1u.83). The detached 'qsm-index build' process reused spawnRunner with the 25 s MCP per-call limit (lib/run.ts CALL_LIMIT_MS), so graphify was stopped on any repository where it needs more; advisor-authorization needs 35.6 s (measured, build ok after the fix run from source). Fix: a buildRunner with a 10-minute limit for the build process, the MCP limit stays on tool calls; spec sentence added. The 'search' timeout half of this issue is separate: search runs semble inside a tool call and must stay under 30 s.

title: qsm-compuse: drive atlas, a headless screen-by-screen design atlas of the desktop
description:
Intent (owner): an automatic tool or test that shoots the whole desktop screen by screen: rest, then 1, 2, 3 windows, then one, two, three random rollouts, then every rollout and every user interface, each with a generated description, like a design per screen; headless if possible; run as a test.
Acceptance: one command runs a scenario file and writes an HTML atlas (screen, item-tree description: surfaces, geometry, contrast, whole-surface check) plus a geometry diff against the previous atlas (no pixel diffs: GPU noise); never touches the owner's session; leaves no process or file behind.
Probe result 2026-10-22: Hyprland 0.56 has no headless mode but runs nested. In sway or cage it aborts (xdg_wm_base 5 < 6). In niri it starts but niri never maps its window. In headless weston 15 (pixman) it runs: the desktop loaded with 0 errors and 3 real foot windows sat on a workspace. Two blockers: (1) SAFETY: with LIBSEAT_BACKEND=noop the nested Aquamarine also started its DRM backend on the real card (/dev/dri/card1) and listed eDP-1 and HDMI-A-1; with logind it tried to take the owner's seat and failed only because it was busy. The nested compositor must run where no card node exists (bwrap with only the render node bound) before anything else. (2) CAPTURE: grim on the nested Hyprland says 'failed to create buffer'; try weston --debug with weston-screenshooter, or a GL renderer. Probe scripts: ~/.cache/qsm-night-2026-10-21/tools (copy hyprprobe/weston.sh, nested.sh, min.conf, niri.kdl). Fallback if blocked: the sway slot atlas (all rollouts and UI, no workspaces or windows) plus live shots of window states by the main agent.

comments.author: qs_m4rk
comments.text: Owner additions (2026-10-22): (1) keep the history of every atlas run; (2) a pixel and area diff between screenshots, but only between the same named shot of two runs, so the scenario is a DEFINED set, never randomized (the earlier 'random rollouts' is replaced by a fixed list); (3) simple journeys like Playwright: named step lists (open, hover, click, key, expect) whose every step is a named shot. Notes: AGENTS.md struck pixel diffing because the same scene differs by GPU noise, so the diff needs a per-channel tolerance and reports changed AREAS (connected regions over a size), and the scenario must freeze what changes with time (clock, notification ages, battery, wallpaper animation) before shots are comparable. niri in the probe was only a parent compositor to host the nested Hyprland (sway and cage speak an older xdg-shell), never the desktop under test.

blocked" in the skill, but blocked comes from the browserbox driver.

Decided (user, 2026-10-09):

- Per-tool skills: browserbox (takeover, fill-secret, 429 pacing), searxng, opensrc, context7, tavily.

title: qsm-secrets: full key management through one CLI, every other door blocked
description:
Intent: the person and the agent manage and use every secret through qsm-secrets alone. The agent never needs secret-tool, rbw, D-Bus or a keyring file, so every one of those doors is blocked for it, not only the ones that print a value. Why now: today's session needed raw secret-tool pipes typed by the person to rename a captured npm token, migrate old entries and delete junk, and raw D-Bus reads crashed gnome-keyring 11 times.

Not decided yet (grilling): the exact verb set. Candidates seen today:
- rename / mv: give a captured cap_<hex> a real name (qsm/npm-token), across namespaces.
- capture names: let a pasted secret carry a name instead of cap_<hex>.
- list / inspect / rm across every namespace, capture included (today they miss it; likely cause: entries() in lib/libsecret.ts reads key before namespace).
- prune: remove captures that no template or session uses.
- a check verb that runs a consumer to prove a key still works (npm whoami) without printing it.
- capture false positives on file paths: qsm-i1u.27.

Blocking (allowlist, not denylist): the guard today blocks reads only (rbw/bw get, secret-tool lookup/search, pass show, file readers). Target: deny every secret-store tool and door except the qsm-secrets binary itself: secret-tool (all verbs), rbw/bw, pass, busctl/gdbus/dbus-send against org.freedesktop.secrets, keyring and vault files (~/.local/share/keyrings, rbw data), language bindings (python keyring/secretstorage, node keytar). Open: how the person still runs raw tools when needed (the ! prefix is the person, not the agent).

Acceptance (draft): the four tasks from today (rename a capture, migrate an old entry, delete junk, list every namespace) run through qsm-secrets verbs only, and each raw door above is denied with a message that names the qsm-secrets verb to use instead. Related: askpass epic qsm-3gl.

Unverified: whether the hook engine can rewrite the result of every tool (Read, Grep, MCP), not only Bash; prove it first. Known limit: a re-encoded value (base64) is not masked.

title: qsm-secrets: the guard allows only qsm-secrets to reach a secret store
description: Phase 3. Today the guard denies a few readers by regex, quote-unaware, with bypasses (sudo/command prefixes, rbw code, bw export, tac/sed/base64 on credential files). Move the decision into a verb, qsm-secrets guard, that parses the command with shell-ast inside the binary (the hook sandbox cannot load it, unverified) and is called from the hook through $.process.run. Deny: secret-tool (every verb), rbw, bw, pass, busctl/gdbus/dbus-send on org.freedesktop.secrets, keyring and vault files, python keyring/secretstorage, node keytar, printers of a rendered config file. Each denial names the qsm-secrets verb to use. Decision (user): the person runs raw tools in their own terminal; there is no agent exception. Read, Grep and Glob get the same file rule.
acceptance_criteria: Each door in the list is denied with the verb to use, including behind sudo, command, env and a subshell; qsm-secrets itself and ordinary commands pass; Read of ~/.local/share/keyrings is denied.

title: Make qsm-web a simple server-configured production CLI
description: Intent: For the maintainer and coding agents, make the existing qsm-web CLI reliable for web research without duplicating SearXNG server policy in a client file. User approved targeted reconstruction and autonomous completion followed by a report. Preserve useful browserbox, opensrc and upstream integrations. Start from local source, existing specs, real CLI tests and two independent model audits. Delete only verified dead, duplicate or superseded paths, with no compatibility layer. The server owns search defaults; --instance or QSM_SEARXNG_INSTANCE selects its address, and explicit flags override individual requests. Keep partial search warnings and useful results; distinguish unusable output from success. Out of scope: server changes, private config/credential edits, wholesale rewrite, enterprise features, live audio tests, paused model evals. Acceptance: no client config-file or interactive search-setup reader/writer remains; unflagged search does not force engines or other server policy; explicit request flags are validated and honored; result mapping retains useful search/media evidence; partial/empty/all-failed/malformed/unreachable paths have truthful outcomes; affected docs, skills, manifests and generated contracts agree; CLI integration tests, validation and bounded live text/image/Stack Overflow/npm checks run, with npm upstream limitations reported; reviewed findings are fixed or explicitly bounded; independent final review and report name remaining blockers. Budget: minimal targeted changes, no new dependencies or abstraction layers without a demonstrated need.

All three epic tasks closed, final1832 ordinary+108hook tests and whole-root langdev passed with no bypass, bounded live search and installed CLI smoke recorded, finished worktree removed. title: qsm-web: review remaining SearXNG tabs for search profiles
description:
The owner wants the remaining SearXNG catalog reviewed in parallel with GLM researchers, using the bounded evidence process already used for IT. The output is an evidence-backed recommendation for each remaining tab, not new profiles or server changes.

## Done when

- Existing dated evidence is reused explicitly; fresh public queries are isolated to one registered engine and paced through one provider-aware queue.
- Each row distinguishes measured returned links, useful result shape, empty/inconclusive results, provider restrictions, unmet prerequisites and owner exclusions.
- Each tab has a proposed candidate set or a named reason it cannot become a profile; Other remains a Preferences grouping.
- One independent review checks coverage, attribution, evidence and recommendation consistency.

## Not in this task
No server settings, catalog pruning, new API keys/accounts, login, challenge bypass, downloads, model eval runs, implementation or profile installation. One live query per eligible engine at most; stop sibling-provider probes after a challenge/rate-limit and retain every excluded or untested engine in the evidence. Instance-specific evidence stays outside the public repository and tracker.

title: qsm-langdev: a target time per checker at edit, commit, push and CI, a 5-minute timeout only for a stuck process
description:
Intent: every qsm-langdev checker has a target time per point that it is meant to finish under, and a single 5-minute timeout that only catches a stuck process. A run over its target is reported as slow with its measured time, never as a failure; a checker that is over its target consistently is a cause to look at.

Decided by the owner on 2026-10-30, per ONE checker:
- edit: 5 s
- commit: 30 s
- push: 1 min
- CI: 10 min
- timeout: 5 min for everything langdev runs in Claude Code

The owner's words: "Chci ideal time to complete, per ONE checker. Pro edit to je 5s ... Potom u vseho co mame tady na claude code, chci aby to melo 5MIN timout, kdyz se to upe posere, a kdyz to konzistentne over the limit of its X seconds, tak se na to podivame. Ale nechci aby vadilo, ze to treba najednou pojede 30s misto 5s." Commit: "target time for each tool pro commit je 30s. Kdyz to je pod super." Push: "je to target 1 min, timeout 5mins jako vsechno ostatni pro langdev." CI: 10 min.

Also from the owner: "jak je mozne ze commit a edit trvaji stejne dlouho, vsak mame edit profile, a commit profile, tak se to musi cele opravit." Today the code has two points only (lib/registry.ts:153, pre-commit and pre-push); the edit hook runs the pre-commit set.

Measured 2026-10-30 (cold store): edit .ts 16.0-18.2 s at load 13-18 (semgrep-ts not measured at 4-5 s every run; the engine gives the edit call 10 s), edit .md 4.6-6.0 s, stop 9.4 s, commit hook 5.2-9.3 s, push langdev 12.8 s, whole pre-push 10.3 s with the store warm, CI green runs 244-371 s (last green 2026-10-21; red since).

title: qsm-web: choose search sources with simple profiles
description:
## Plain summary
People and agents currently repeat engine lists when switching between everyday search, personal websites and discussions, and academic publications. Add named per-query profiles to the existing SearXNG search command without changing server settings.

## Done when
- The default profile and calls without a profile use server defaults.
- The niche profile selects searchmysite, wiby, mwmbl, and boardreader.

Script for the agent (paste as the prompt):

7. Run `git pull --rebase`. Expect a refusal naming `git pull --rebase=merges`.
8. Make the upstream one commit ahead (commit and push from a second clone), then run `git push`. Expect a refusal naming `git pull --rebase=merges`.
9. Report `wc -c ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ~/.claude/rules/context.md ~/.claude/rules/git.md`.

title: Rewrite: one Claude marketplace, MVP pass 1
description:
Rewrite qsm-marketplace as ONE Claude marketplace: every capability is one plugin that carries its
code, its CLI, its skills, its hooks and its docs together. No tools/, no adapters/. Decided
2026-09-10 with the user, in a grilling round of 13 questions; nothing below is open.

THE USER'S SCOPE, quoted: "Celkove mene docs, mene tests, mene textu. Takze idealne u kazde veci
vzit co tak generarly asi mela delat, a udelat minimal MVP te veci, to bude first pass. Cely
marketplace, no tests, no docs, super simple prompts, MVPs." Docs clarified: must-have docs stay
(README, INSTALL + USAGE for a plugin with a bin, specs), everything explanatory or historical goes.
Specs clarified: EVERY plugin gets openspec/specs in phase 0, written by agents as "super simple MVP
feature-full" specs from the old plugin, and the build follows the spec plus the old plugin as
reference.

SETTLED DECISIONS
1. Re-author, not git mv: each plugin is written again with the old tree as reference; every file
   is reviewed. No test is carried over; pass 1 has no tests. Behaviour tests come in pass 2, per
   plugin, once the MVP shows which behaviour deserves one.
2. Layout: repo root is the marketplace. `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at root, plugins under
   `plugins/<name>/`. A plugin holds `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `qsm.json` (bin + commands, only
   when it ships a CLI), `lib/`, `scripts/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `hooks/`, `openspec/`,
   `README.md`, and `INSTALL.md` + `USAGE.md` only when it ships a bin. The old rule "root plugins/
   is not live source" is inverted: plugins/ IS the source.
3. Shared code lives in root `lib/` outside every plugin: install-contract and the hook build
   helper, nothing else in pass 1 (test helpers do not move, there are no tests). A plugin never
   imports from another plugin; root lib/ is layer 0, plugins/ layer 1. Claude docs describe plugins
   as self-contained and have no sharing convention; this works because our scripts run from the
   repo and hooks are compiled binaries with imports baked in.
4. Language plugins qsm-langdev-{ts,py,dotnet,shell,zsh,fish} stay separate plugins, skills only,
   each declaring `qsm.requires: ["qsm-langdev"]` so the tool installs first and a project adds
   only its languages. Per-language dev notes land there in pass 2.
5. Drops: qsm-cloakbrowser, qsm-skyvern, qsm-stagehand (parked) are not rewritten. qsm-lsp-adapter
   (empty), qsm-claude-lsp-adapter and qsm-csharp-lsp merge into ONE plugin `qsm-lsp`. Any further
   drop: the user closes that plugin's spec bead with the reason; that is the inventory.
6. Prompts: SKILL.md at most 8 KB, one file per skill, one file per agent, no `references/`
   directories in pass 1. Iron Law 5's 48 KB cap becomes 8 KB for skills and agents.
7. Gates in the rewrite worktree: `.qsm-langdev/gates.json` selects `secrets` and `entropy` only,
   until qsm-langdev and qsm-sentrux are rebuilt; then their gates return.
8. Provisioning: branch `rewrite` in a worktree, main frozen except hotfixes, beads DB shared from
   the main checkout (verified: `br list` from a worktree sees the same 102 open issues). One bead
   per plugin per phase; the USER closes a build bead after review, never the agent.
9. The sentrux fork patch (tools/qsm-sentrux/sentrux-0.5.7-qsm.patch, 14 files) is carried byte
   for byte: it is upstream's code plus about 60 lines of ours, not ours to simplify.
10. Workers: sonnet subagents, one plugin per dispatch, in the rewrite worktree; haiku only for
    quick doc writes. The orchestrator reviews before the user does.

PHASES
- Phase 0 (specs): one bead per plugin. Read the old plugin (tools/<name> and
  adapters/claude/modules/<name> on main), write plugins/<name>/openspec/specs as a super simple MVP
  feature-full spec: what it does, its verbs/skills/hooks, its failure behaviour. Nothing about how.
  The user approves each spec by closing the bead.
- Phase 1 (foundation): worktree, wipe, survivors, root lib/, marketplace.json, gates.json,
  AGENTS.md v2, rules.toml, validators. Details in its bead.
- Phase 2 (build): one bead per plugin, depends on its spec bead and on the foundation bead;
  qsm-langdev-* also on qsm-langdev. Acceptance is in each bead.
- Phase 3 (parity + merge): every kept surface installs and runs once by hand, `bun run validate`
  green, gates back on, merge rewrite into main, re-add the marketplace to Claude (its root moved).

START HERE, in a fresh session:
  git -C ~/Projects/qsm-marketplace worktree add -b rewrite ~/Projects/qsm-marketplace.rewrite main
  cd ~/Projects/qsm-marketplace.rewrite
Then take the Phase 0 beads. Disable the user-scope qsm-langdev and qsm-sentrux plugins for that
session: on a wiped tree their stop hooks find no profile and log noise. Re-enable when rebuilt.

WHAT THE WIPE KEEPS (root of the worktree): .git, .beads/ (issues.jsonl is tracked and shared,
never delete it), .gitleaks.toml and .secrets.baseline (the two kept gates fail without them),
mise.toml, .gitignore, .claude/ (project settings, commands, skills), .qsm-langdev/gates.json
rewritten to the two gates. Everything else is deleted in the first commit and rebuilt.

THIRTY-ODD PLUGINS ARE THIN WRAPPERS: 20 to 100 lines of code and 200 to 450 lines of prose that
restate the upstream manual, the violation AGENTS.md already names. Their MVP is plugin.json,
qsm.json when they wrap a binary, one README paragraph with the install command and our caveats.
Do not rewrite 400 lines of docs into 300.
